findings.title: `queued` default is evaluated once at import time, not per instance
findings.description: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` runs once when the class body executes. Every `AssignmentSource` built without an explicit `queued` (both `from_integration` at line 22 and the call sites in `src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py:98` and `:115`) carries the process start time, not the time the assignment was queued. Nothing reads `queued` today, so there is no behavioural effect yet, but the field is wrong for any future staleness check or log. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

findings.title: `from_dict` swallows parse failures, silently disabling the cycle guard
findings.description:
`from_dict` returns `None` on any `TypeError`/`ValueError`, and `src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py:53-56` treats `None` as "no source". A malformed payload therefore falls through to a normal outbound sync, which is exactly the sync cycle this change exists to prevent, with no log or metric.
- **Unknown keys:** `cls(**input_dict)` rejects any extra key. If a field is later added to the dataclass, older workers will drop the whole source during a rolling deploy.
- **No type validation:** `{"source_name": 1, "integration_id": "abc"}` builds an instance, and the `integration_id` comparison in `should_sync` then never matches.

Log a warning when a non-empty dict fails to parse, filter to known fields, and validate that `integration_id` is an int.

findings.title: `sync_status_outbound` gains an `assignment_source` parameter that nothing passes or implements
findings.description:
The abstract `sync_status_outbound` now declares `assignment_source`, but the only caller, `src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_status_outbound.py:43-46`, passes neither it nor a `sync_source` to `should_sync("outbound_status")`. No concrete override was updated:
- `src/sentry/integrations/jira/integration.py:990`, `src/sentry/integrations/jira_server/integration.py:1090` and `src/sentry/integrations/vsts/issues.py:266` would absorb it via `**kwargs`.
- `src/sentry/integrations/example/integration.py:161` has no `**kwargs`, so passing the argument would raise `TypeError`, and its signature no longer matches the base.

An "assignment" source on a status method is also a semantic mismatch. Either drop the parameter from this change or wire it through the status task and the overrides.

findings.title: Tests cover only one branch of the new behaviour
findings.description:
The only new behavioural test is assign with a matching source. Missing:
- **Different source integration:** no test that a source from another integration still syncs outbound. This is the property the comment at `src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:387-389` promises, and a regression would silently stop all cross-integration sync.
- **Deassign with matching source:** the new `assignment_source` path in `deassign` (`src/sentry/models/groupassignee.py:238-240`) is untested.
- **Inbound attaches the source:** nothing asserts that `sync_group_assignee_inbound` passes a source (`src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py:96-99`, `:112-116`). The existing inbound tests would pass if those arguments were removed.
- **`should_sync` directly:** no unit test of `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync` with a `sync_source`.
- **Round trip:** `tests/sentry/integrations/services/test_assignment_source.py` has no `from_dict(to_dict())` test, which is the path production uses. `test_to_dict` (lines 29-38) only checks `queued is not None`, so it cannot catch the import-time default.

Minor, same file: `test_from_dict_inalid_data` is a typo (line 13), `test_from_dict_empty_array` tests a dict, and the DB-backed `TestCase` is unnecessary for a pure dataclass.

findings.title: Same concept named `sync_source` and `assignment_source`
findings.description: `should_sync` calls the parameter `sync_source` (lines 66 and 382); everywhere else it is `assignment_source` or `assignment_source_dict`. Pick one name, since `should_sync` is also used for comment and status attributes where "assignment" does not fit.

findings.title: `from_integration` hardcodes the class instead of using `cls`
findings.description: `from_integration` is a `@classmethod` but constructs `AssignmentSource(...)` directly, while `from_dict` at line 33 uses `cls(...)`. Use `cls` in both.

findings.title: Task payload depends on the pickle serializer for the `datetime` field
findings.description: `to_dict()` puts a `datetime` into the Celery kwargs. This works because `CELERY_TASK_SERIALIZER = "pickle"` (`src/sentry/conf/server.py:739`), and a plain dict passes the bad-pickle check in `src/sentry/celery.py:55`. Under a JSON serializer `queued` would come back as a string and `from_dict` would accept it unconverted. Serializing `queued` as ISO-8601 and parsing it in `from_dict` would make the contract explicit.

findings.title: Cycle guard logic and task backward compatibility are sound
findings.description: `should_sync` compares `sync_source.integration_id` with `self.org_integration.integration_id` after the `org_integration is None` guard at line 384, so only the originating integration is suppressed. The new `assignment_source_dict` task argument defaults to `None` (`src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py:34`), so tasks already in the queue still run. All concrete `sync_assignee_outbound` overrides (jira, jira_server, vsts, example) accept `**kwargs`, so the new keyword at line 59-61 is safe. The module-level import in `src/sentry/models/groupassignee.py:15` adds no import cycle: `assignment_source.py` imports only Django at runtime and `src/sentry/integrations/services/__init__.py` is empty.

structured_findings.summary: `queued` default is evaluated once at import time, not per instance
`from_dict` swallows parse failures, silently disabling the cycle guard
`sync_status_outbound` gains an `assignment_source` parameter that nothing passes or implements
Tests cover only one branch of the new behaviour
`from_integration` hardcodes the class instead of using `cls`
Task payload depends on the pickle serializer for the `datetime` field
Cycle guard logic and task backward compatibility are sound
